parameters.content:
## CORE PIPELINE — Newsletter Automation
Runs weekly (Monday 6am). Ingests → dedupes → ranks → generates → verifies → routes to Slack for human approval → sends segmented campaigns on approval.

Sibling workflows (separate, independent, do NOT merge these back in):
→ Newsletter Automation - Health Check (daily monitoring)
→ Newsletter Automation - Pruning (weekly maintenance)

Full reasoning for every major decision: TECHNICAL-DECISIONS.md

## Ingestion
Feeds live in Airtable (Feed config table), not hardcoded add/remove a source by editing data, not this workflow.

RSS Read has Continue-on-Fail enabled one dead feed won't halt the run.

##  Ranking
Groq primary (many small calls = RPM-bound), Gemini fallback. Throttled via Loop+Wait between calls.

Model IDs get deprecated without warning  if this starts 404ing, check the model name first before anything else.

##  Generation & Verification
Generates grounded newsletter JSON, then runs it through two-tier Content Verification before saving:
- Tier 1 (deterministic, every run): flags numeric/version claims not found in source text
- Tier 2 (LLM, only if Tier 1 flags something): semantic judgment call on the flagged claims

Full JSON saved to Airtable's Newsletter Content field — this is what lets Approve/Reject work correctly even days after generation, once this execution no longer exists.

## Slack Approval Request
Uses HTTP Request calling chat.postMessage directly — NOT the native n8n Slack node. That node silently dropped every Block Kit button across multiple tested variations.
Do not swap back without re-verifying this first.

Requires: Slack App → Interactivity ON, Request URL = this workflow's webhook Production URL. Method must be POST. Content-Type header must be set explicitly.

## Webhook Intake & Routing
Slack sends the click as form-encoded data with the real payload nested as a JSON STRING inside body.payload — must be JSON.parse()'d, never arrives as an object directly.

Switch is in Rules mode matching string values (approve/edit/reject), not Expression mode with an index.

## Approve → Segmented Send
One newsletter, re-angled per segment (not regenerated) keeps facts fixed and consistent, keeps cost roughly linear.

Brevo auth header is "api-key" (lowercase, no Bearer prefix) completely different pattern from Slack's credential. Don't reuse the Slack one here.

Create-campaign and send-now are TWO separate API calls. Sender email must show Verified in Brevo or every send fails.

## Reject & Edit Requested
Both are manual dead-ends by design  no automation resumes until a human acts. Reject doesn't auto-regenerate; next draft comes from the normal Monday schedule.
